findings.evidence: M5 — the PRE-FIX spec (git show fe278a8^:.claude/scripts/tests/design-rollup.test.sh) run against the same shipped qa-gate.sh, with a debug capture at H.3. Observed: approve exit 2, error_key=completion_files_total_miss, observations 'NONE of the 1 declared file(s) are in the change set this approval would bind (declared=1 bound=1 matched=0) ... Declared (first 12 shown): src/a.sh'. The tracker AT THAT MOMENT held exactly one path: docs/specs/<epic>.md. bound=1, not bound=0 — the tracker was NOT empty at H.3.
findings.description: The new comment attributes the pre-fix total miss to the tracker being truncated ('G.1's successful approve TRUNCATES $TRACKING, so by this point ...'). Measured, that is not the operative cause. Section H replaces the tracker wholesale at line 674 (printf '%s\n' "$ART" > "$TRACKING" — a '>' overwrite, not '>>') two steps before H.3, so src/a.sh leaves the bound change set whether or not G.1's approve truncated anything; had truncation been the cause, bound would have been 0 and the empty-tracker/persisted-report path would have applied instead. The sentence's CONCLUSION — a genuine total miss, the q5l6 guard preempting the rollup-staleness check, H.3 measuring the wrong refusal — is TRUE and independently confirmed by the same run, and the fix itself is right. Only the cited cause is wrong. Suggested one-line replacement: 'Section H replaces $TRACKING with the amended design artifact (line ~674), so the change set an approval would bind no longer contains src/a.sh — the only file the epic's recorded completion declares. (G.1's own approve truncates the tracker on success too, but the replacement alone is what produces the miss.)' Classified medium rather than high because the false part is an attributed intermediate step in an explanation, not a statement about shipped behaviour that a reader acts on: the remedy is a comment amendment, and no assertion, exit code, or user-visible claim changes. If 'shipped claim' in the stop rule is read to cover comment prose, this is the one finding in the diff that would be HIGH under that reading.

findings.evidence: The inserted seed uses the path list 'src/b.sh', which is also the path list of the very next call at line 757 (epic_review_and_complete "$EPIC" "3" "src/b.sh"). The helper's own doc comment (lines 354-370) says the file set 'MUST be varied across consecutive calls on the SAME epic' because change_set_hash hashes the PATH LIST alone. In M3b and M3c — where H.3's approve SUCCEEDS because the staleness property was broken — H.6 ('RESTORE CONTROL: approve succeeds once the rollup is fresh again') still PASSED, with hash([src/b.sh]) by then bound to a prior QA-GATE APPROVED record. cmd_approve's IDEMPOTENT-APPROVE-CONFLICT-RECHECK arm returns status=approved, exit 0 (qa-gate.sh ~5635: 'idempotent no-op — nothing rewritten'), and H.6 asserts only .status and the exit code.
findings.description: Not a present defect: today H.3's approve REFUSES, so no approval record binds hash([src/b.sh]) and H.6's success is genuinely attributable to the fresh rollup. It is a latent coupling the file elsewhere goes to great lengths to avoid — Section K's own 'ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING' comment documents this exact wrong-reason pass, measured. Suggested v5.0.1 hardening: give the inserted seed a path list no other round uses (for example '.claude/scripts/tests/dr-u2.test.sh', declared by U2, and never used as a path list elsewhere in this file), so H.6's control stays discriminating even if H.3's expectation ever changes.

findings.evidence: cmd_review_record reads the iteration from the piped JSON — iter=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | jq -r '.iterations') — and derives the canonical path via review_artifact_path_for "$tid" "$iter" = $PROJECT_DIR/$REVIEW_ARTIFACT_SUBDIR/<tid>-r<iterations>.json. epic_review_and_complete hardcodes "iterations":1 in every artifact it writes and pipes it on stdin (< "$eart"), never --file. seed_review_and_enter is only ever called on CHILD tasks (line 433), so no other r1 artifact exists for this epic.
findings.description: The commit's 'review iterations renumbered to stay unique' is an accurate description of the edit, but the renumbering is inert: the $iter argument names only the staging file under .claude/.qa-tracking/, while every recorded artifact carries iteration=1 and lands at docs/reviews/<epic>-r1.json. No iteration collision was possible before the renumber and none exists after. Noted so a future reader does not treat the numbering as load-bearing state.
